Anduril founder Palmer Luckey on AI making life-and-death decisions without human approval:
I think it is the only rational moral outcome or decision to make. 
Life-and-death decisions are too morally fraught and too important to not bring to bear the most powerful technology that you have.

Bernie Sanders:
Rosa Luxemburg was a socialist leader. She was Polish, actually, but worked in Germany.
What she said is either we will have socialism or barbarism.
Either people will, in a sense, learn to live together and work together, or else we're going to end up having [barbarism].
The struggle that we have is to bring out the better angels of people rather than the worst parts of humanity, the ugliest parts.

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey:
If you had an autonomous landmine that could differentiate between a Russian tank and a school bus full of kids, there are people in the world who seriously argue that it is better to have a dumb mine that blows up that school bus full of kids as long as it wasn't a robot who decided who lived and who died. 
I just can't abide by that.

Bernie Sanders on Elon Musk:
I don't know what happened to Musk over the years. I talked to him once in my life, and that was a long time ago.
This is a guy who was concerned about climate change and was maybe the leading voice in creating electric vehicles, Tesla and so forth and so on. 
I think he was close to Obama. So I don't know what ended up happening.
I can respect him as a smart and aggressive businessman. I cannot respect in any way, shape or form what he is doing politically.
